daily_brief: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz faces mounting political pressure after his CDU party suffered historic defeats in two state elections Sunday, failing to enter parliament in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern for the first time in 77 years while the far-right AfD surged [BBC, Le Monde, France 24]. Russia's parliamentary elections delivered an expected victory for United Russia, expanding its constitutional majority despite over four years of war in Ukraine, with the only anti-war party Yabloko barred from the ballot [BBC, The Hindu]. Ukraine launched its largest drone attack on Moscow, with 450 drones targeting the capital's oil refinery and causing civilian casualties, as President Trump reportedly pressures Kyiv to halt strikes on Russian energy infrastructure [BBC, France 24, Financial Times]. In Ethiopia, seven armed groups including the TPLF and Fano militias formed an unprecedented alliance seeking to overthrow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government, raising fears of renewed civil war [BBC, RFI]. Three major US news outlets—CNN, Politico, and MS NOW—announced they will sue the Trump administration over their White House ban, citing First Amendment violations [BBC, Financial Times]. World leaders gather in New York for the UN General Assembly, with key bilateral meetings expected between Trump and leaders including Macron, Burnham, and Zelensky amid ongoing conflicts in Iran and Ukraine [Globe and Mail, RFI].

top_stories.headline: German Chancellor Merz Vows to Stay On Despite CDU's Historic State Election Defeats
bullets: CDU fell below 5% threshold in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, failing to enter a state parliament for first time in 77 years
Far-right AfD won 37% in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern; Die Linke (The Left) led in Berlin with CDU dropping to second place
Merz called results a 'disaster' but pledged to continue with economic, tax, and welfare reform agenda
AfD co-leader Alice Weidel told BBC that Merz would leave office 'pretty soon'

top_stories.headline: Russia's United Russia Party Expands Parliamentary Majority as Anti-War Opposition Barred
bullets: United Russia won 57.83% of vote, up from 49.8% in 2021, securing approximately 355 of 450 Duma seats
Elections held after four-and-a-half years of war in Ukraine, amid economic difficulties and fuel shortages from Ukrainian drone strikes
Anti-war party Yabloko was removed from the ballot by Supreme Court just 12 days after being registered
Yabloko appeared to win a small foothold only in one regional parliament

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Emphasized Kremlin control and suppression of dissent, noting lack of surprises

sources.framing_note: More detailed on vote counts and constitutional implications of majority

top_stories.headline: Ukraine Launches Largest Drone Attack on Moscow, Hitting Oil Refinery
bullets: Mayor Sobyanin said 450 drones were shot down in 'most massive' attack on Moscow region
Strikes hit Moscow's main oil refinery and a residential building; at least two killed and 20 injured in Moscow region
President Zelensky confirmed hits on 'key' Russian oil facility and logistics site worth 'billions of dollars'
Financial Times reports Trump pressuring Zelensky to stop strikes on Russian refineries

sources.framing_note: Balanced coverage of both Ukrainian and Russian perspectives on casualties

sources.framing_note: Brief coverage noting timing coincided with Russian election

top_stories.headline: Seven Ethiopian Armed Groups Form Alliance to Overthrow Abiy Ahmed Government
bullets: Alliance called 'Alliance for Survival' includes TPLF, Fano militia, Oromo Liberation Army, and four smaller groups
Groups accuse government of 'war, genocide, mass destruction, and utter poverty' and warn Ethiopia risks disintegration
Former enemies now collaborating after over a year of discussions; Fano leader Zemene Kasse to chair alliance
African Union has noted troop buildups along Tigray border; previous civil war killed approximately 600,000 people

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Factual coverage noting groups span half of Ethiopia's regional states

sources.name: RFI
sources.framing_note: Emphasized TPLF vice president quotes and risk of return to war that killed 600,000

top_stories.headline: CNN, Politico, and MS NOW to Sue Trump Administration Over White House Press Ban
bullets: Three outlets announced joint lawsuit Monday after being barred from White House on Friday
Reporters had credentials revoked and badges seized when attempting to access building Saturday
Trump cited 'fiction or lies' about his government but did not specify particular stories
Outlets claim ban violates First Amendment protections against government discrimination based on coverage content

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Straightforward reporting on legal and constitutional issues

sources.name: Financial Times
sources.framing_note: Brief headline coverage, limited additional context
